relations: _inherit: res.partner; adds street_name, street_number, street_number2 (Char), city_id->res.city, country_enforce_cities (related res.country.enforce_cities)

behavioral_notes.observation: The three structured sub-fields are stored, computed-with-inverse Char fields. _compute_street_data fires on every change of the combined `street` and splits it into its parts by calling tools.street_split(partner.street). The split is driven by tools.ADDRESS_REGEX = r'^(.*?)(\s[0-9][0-9\S]*)?(?: - (.+))?$': street_name = leading text, street_number = first whitespace-delimited token beginning with a digit, street_number2 = the part after ' - '. Storing both the raw `street` and the parsed components is invisible to field metadata; only reading the compute reveals that the canonical source of truth remains `street` and the sub-fields are derived.

Bidirectional sync: when street_name, street_number or street_number2 are written directly (e.g. from a structured input form), _inverse_street_data rejoins them back into `street` as ((street_name or '') + ' ' + (street_number or '')).strip(), appending ' - ' + street_number2 when present. This split-on-read / join-on-write mirror keeps the legacy single `street` field and the structured fields consistent in both directions, so any module reading plain `street` still works while structured countries get the parsed parts. The join template is hard-coded here (it does not consult res.country); only the inverse direction is symmetric with the regex used on compute.

The module adds a Boolean enforce_cities on res.country and a city_id Many2one(res.city) plus a related country_enforce_cities on res.partner. For countries flagged enforce_cities, addresses are expected to pick a city from the curated res.city list; _onchange_city_id then copies the chosen city's name, zipcode and state_id onto the partner's city/zip/state_id (one-way master-data fill-down), and _onchange_country_id clears city_id when the partner's country no longer matches the city's country. city_id is registered as an address field via _address_fields() so it propagates on contact/child-address creation. These cross-field side-effects are not derivable from metadata.

Whether the structured street fields are surfaced is country-driven: res.country carries address_format (Text, 'Layout in Reports') and address_view_id (alternate input form); res.partner._get_address_format() falls back to _get_default_address_format() '%(street)s
%(street2)s
%(city)s %(state_code)s %(zip)s
%(country_name)s' when no country format is set, and get_address_fields()/_check_address_format() validate the format keys against the partner formatting fields. So the 'countries that need it' targeting is realised through the country's address_format / address_view_id, while base_address_extended supplies the street_name/street_number/street_number2 parsing those formats can reference.

base_address_extended ships no client-side code: extract_frontend reports present=false, 0 JS files, 0 XML/OWL templates, 0 registry adds, 0 patches, 0 services, no asset bundles. The structured-street and city UX is delivered purely through inherited server-side XML form/list/search views (form=1, list=1, search=1) over the standard web client; there is no bespoke OWL widget.

it_architecture.application: base_address_extended (address master-data structuring utility extending res.partner / res.country)
software_services: (no HTTP routes; exposes ORM-level compute/inverse and onchange behaviour on res.partner consumed in-process by the contacts/address UI and any module reading partner addresses)
information_flows: depends: [base, contacts] (extends the base partner/country master data and the Contacts app)
side-effect: write street -> _compute_street_data splits into street_name/street_number/street_number2 (tools.ADDRESS_REGEX)
side-effect: write any street sub-field -> _inverse_street_data rejoins into street ('name number - number2')
side-effect: select city_id -> _onchange_city_id fills city/zip/state_id from res.city; change country -> _onchange_country_id clears mismatched city_id
config: res.country.enforce_cities / address_format / address_view_id govern whether structured/city input is required and shown per country

capabilities: Structure Partner Street Address (split/join street into street name, number, door)
Maintain Curated City Master Data (res.city per country/state)
Enforce Country-Specific Address Rules (enforce_cities, address_format/view per country)
Auto-fill Address Components from City selection (city/zip/state)
value_streams: Address-Capture-to-Structured-Record: user types a combined street (or picks a city) -> module parses/joins components and fills city/zip/state -> a normalized, country-conformant partner address ready for reuse across CRM/Sales/Invoicing/Shipping
information_concepts: res.partner (contact address, extended with structured street + city_id)
policies: res.country.enforce_cities flag — requires choosing a city from the curated list for flagged countries
res.country.address_format constraint (_check_address_format) validating layout format keys
stakeholders: Sales / Invoicing / Delivery users relying on structured addresses
Localization (l10n) modules requiring per-country street/city structuring

classification.rationale: base_address_extended owns no business object of its own: it is a thin extension of existing master data (res.partner, res.country) plus one reference-data model (res.city) whose entire job is to improve the structure and quality of address data — splitting/rejoining the partner street into street_name/street_number/street_number2 and enforcing curated cities per country. By Stabell & Fjeldstad this is a 'support' value model (firm infrastructure / data management), never a primary value-creating activity; it produces no document chain and confirms/transforms no business state. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' is chosen as the master-data / data-quality home for this utility (an argument exists for 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' as it refines the shared Information-Concept of a partner address, but the dominant character is data-structuring infrastructure, so 8.0 is primary). activity_class=support and the absence of routes/groups/business value-streams confirm the classification.

standard_capabilities: structured street fields (street_name, street_number, street_number2) computed from / inverted to the combined street via tools.street_split
bidirectional sync keeping legacy single `street` consistent with the structured components
curated city master data (res.city) with country/state/zip and display name
per-country enforcement of city selection (res.country.enforce_cities) with auto-fill of city/zip/state
country-driven address layout (address_format) and alternate input form (address_view_id) selecting which structured fields appear
typical_fits: localizations needing house/door numbers split out of the street (e.g. many EU countries)
deployments wanting validated city lists rather than free-text city entry
reports/labels that must render addresses in a country-specific structured layout
common_gaps: loading/maintaining the res.city reference data per country (often supplied by l10n_* modules)
the split regex assumes a 'name number - number2' convention; countries with number-first formats may need custom parsing or a dedicated address_view_id
address validation / geocoding / postal-code lookup (separate add-ons such as base_address_city, partner_autocomplete)
drive_hints: odoo shell: p = env['res.partner'].create({'street': 'Main Street 12 - B'}); (p.street_name, p.street_number, p.street_number2)  # ('Main Street','12','B')
odoo shell: env['res.country'].search([('enforce_cities','=',True)])  # countries requiring a curated city
odoo shell: env['res.city'].search_count([])  # number of curated cities loaded

open_questions: Which countries ship enforce_cities=True and how much res.city reference data is actually loaded (depends on installed l10n_* modules).
How robust the ADDRESS_REGEX split is for non-'name number - number2' conventions (number-first or comma-separated formats).
Whether downstream apps (Sales/Invoicing/Delivery/website checkout) consume street_name/street_number directly or only the combined street.
